scope: D1 read-path remediation history and current learning-page latency diagnosis

structuralChanges: User lookup, rate-limit update, unread count, and route data were grouped into D1 batches.
The first jobs route received a dedicated bootstrap payload for user, unread count, categories, and data.
Job rows and total count were executed in one D1 batch.
The full active catalog was hydrated once and filtering, sorting, searching, calendar movement, and paging became browser-memory operations.
The jobs route chunk was preloaded before route entry.
Feed and category indexes removed avoidable sorting and broad scans.

currentProductionLearningData.source: Sites live D1 bounded table reads

currentProductionLearningLatency.source: Sites Worker logs, successful HTTP 200 requests only

controlledLearningBenchmark.interpretation: The artificial delay exposes D1 dispatch waves only; it is not a production latency claim.

inAppNavigation: lazy LearningPage module load when not already cached

libraryRead.note: The context statements and one JSON-aggregating learning statement share a single D1 batch.

waves: flashcards, questions, and attempts SELECTs in parallel

primary: Unit detail performs five D1 dispatches across three sequential waves.
Learning direct entry has no dedicated bootstrap, so authentication and learning data are separate requests.
LearningPage remains a lazy-only route and is not proactively preloaded like JobsPage.
secondary: The detail response is fetched only after a card is clicked; no hover, focus, or first-source prefetch is used.
The attempts query index begins with user_id and question_id while the query filters user_id plus the joined unit_id; this is a future scale risk, not the current bottleneck.
notCurrentRootCause: The selected detail response is 2558 bytes in the controlled benchmark.
Worker CPU is 3 to 4 ms for the observed 536 to 548 ms detail requests.
Current production has zero learning question attempts.
Learning images use lazy loading and do not explain the API wait before detail data arrives.

priority: Create a learning bootstrap that returns user, unread count, and the learning library in one request and one D1 batch for direct /learning entry.
Convert unit detail into one fast read plan that batches context, unit, flashcards, questions, and attempts in one D1 dispatch.
Preload LearningPage with the same resilient promise pattern used by JobsPage.
After dispatch consolidation, measure whether intent-based detail prefetch is still necessary.
Add or revise the attempts index only if EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN and larger attempt fixtures show a scan.
recommendedNextDesign.latencyPromise: No production latency reduction is claimed until the design is implemented and measured under the same conditions.

limitations: The production learning-library sample count is one in the selected log window.
The browser automation session was not authenticated, so no private page DOM or browser resource timing was captured.
Production logs establish Worker wall and CPU time but do not expose a per-statement D1 breakdown.
Controlled benchmark timings exclude internet, browser rendering, asset download, and production D1 latency.
No learning performance fix is included in this diagnosis-only change.
